Top 5 recorded entries:

# Interactive daemon manager

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph ships `codegraph daemon` with alias `daemons` as an interactive manager for background daemons, showing the current project first and allowing stop-one or stop-all. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says this replaces hunting for a pid and killing it by hand.

# Project-local config auto-wiring

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph init` auto-wires project-local agent configuration for agents previously installed globally, so a global install applies in each opened project without per-project reinstall. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.7.7 says one global `codegraph install` works in every project you open because `codegraph init` wires project-local agent config for globally installed agents.

# Value-ref false-positive handling

Lifecycle status: accepted

During value-reference validation, false-positive clusters must be fixed while isolated singletons are recorded as known residuals. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §0 instructs agents to hunt FPs during the validation sweep, fix FP clusters, and record singletons.

# Project-name-neutral intent ranking

Lifecycle status: accepted

Search ranking should not let a repo-wide project name overpower the query terms that identify the actual code area. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#5 says users naturally include the project name in queries, but it over-weighted matching paths and buried the backend in mixed-stack repos until project-name terms were neutralized for path scoring and type-disambiguation bias.

# Cursor explicit project path

Lifecycle status: accepted

The installer passes the correct project path into Cursor's MCP config so globally installed CodeGraph resolves the workspace even when Cursor launches MCP servers with the wrong working directory. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.7.7 Fixes says this works around Cursor launching MCP servers with the wrong working directory and fixes global installs reporting `not initialized` in every workspace.

Lifecycle status: proposed

# Arrow callback link-through

Lifecycle status: proposed

Callback synthesis should handle anonymous-arrow handlers by parsing the arrow body and linking the dispatcher to calls inside the arrow. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Remaining work item 1 marks this as the highest remaining recall win for `on('e', () => foo())`.

Lifecycle status: accepted

Dynamic-dispatch work follows a real difficulty gradient: named-reference dispatch is cheap resolver work, anonymous callback dispatch is medium synthesizer work, and anonymous-arrow handlers are the hard remaining gap because they have no identity and require link-through-body synthesis. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#6 states this gradient directly under Known limits and gotchas.

Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#1 Step 3 says named inline handlers are handled by generic extraction, while anonymous handlers need synthesizer link-through-body and are not yet built.
